subject: C-suite briefing: decision criteria, procurement track, and open escalations
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stratifyhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@stratifyhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from Wed exec call — quick summary and asks

Olga / team — thanks for the concise briefing today. Quick recap from our side so we can be aligned before we take this up internally with Finance/Legal: 

- Primary business outcome: reduce inference costs for customer-facing conversational flows by ~40% while keeping median latency under 250ms at P95.
- Why this matters: our product team needs predictable per-call economics for 2027 ARR planning; current vendor costs are highly variable and impacting margin.
- Key risk for leadership: data residency and auditability (we host PHI-adjacent metadata in us-west).
- Procurement preference: marketplace purchase (preferred) OR 12-month SOW + PO if legal needs it.
- Budget signal: we have headroom in Q1 2027 but we need an executable SOW and a clear runbook for failover.

Open questions from our CFO/GC:
1) Can you provide SOC 2 artifacts and a short note on how Private deployment would look for us (VPC, KMS, audit logs)?
2) If we go reserved capacity, what's the exit/scale-down flexibility?
3) Will you commit to a 99.9% inference availability SLA for the Dedicated offering?

We'd like a short, one-page exec brief (business outcomes, procurement path, top 3 risks + mitigations) to show the CFO this week. Can you turn that around?

Thanks — Tom
Tom Nguyen | CFO, Stratify Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stratifyhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@stratifyhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: C-suite one-pager and short answers to your CFO/GC questions

Tom / Priya — attached is the one-page executive brief and a short Q&A that addresses the CFO/GC items you raised. Summary highlights below (full brief attached):

Business outcomes (one-line): deliver a 35–45% reduction in per-call inference spend vs. your current vendor while keeping P95 latency <= 250ms through a production pilot and targeted quantization + caching recommendations.

Procurement track options (recommended order):
1) Marketplace SKU (fastest, low legal friction) — recommended if your legal accepts our standard Marketplace terms; supports immediate pilot.
2) 12-month SOW + PO (Enterprise) — allows custom SLAs, reserved capacity & pricing. Typical cadence: SOW + PO signed → 2-week onboarding → 8–12 week pilot.

Top risks + mitigations:
- Data residency / audit logs: Private control plane + customer-managed VPC + KMS. We’ll provide SOC 2 artifacts and a one-page architecture diagram for your GC. (Attachment: SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf; architecture-diagram.png)
- Performance regression vs baseline: canary pilot with rollback and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant.
- Procurement timeline compression: offer a limited-time pilot credit and a built-in 30-day termination clause in the pilot SOW to reduce risk.

Answers to the specific CFO/GC questions: 
1) SOC2 artifacts: attached, and we can provide an encrypted bundle to your legal team.
2) Exit/scale-down flexibility: Reserved capacity contracts include a 30% minimum commitment for the first quarter and prorated scale-down thereafter with 60 days notice. We can propose more flexible terms in the Enterprise SOW.
3) SLA: For Dedicated we typically offer 99.9% monthly inference availability; for Marketplace we provide best-effort SLAs with optional paid SLA add-on. Dedicated SLA details are available in the SOW.

Next steps we propose:
- 12/02 10:00–10:30AM PT: contract workshop (Finance + Legal + Tech). Can you confirm?
- We’ll share the redline-friendly SOW and a short pilot playbook by 12/01 COB.

Attachments: Exec_brief_onepager.pdf (generated), SOW_draft_v1.pdf, SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf, architecture-diagram.png

Best,
Olga
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0194

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@stratifyhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stratifyhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: C-suite one-pager and short answers to your CFO/GC questions

Thanks, Olga — received and already helpful. A couple of clarifications from Legal: 
- For the Marketplace option, can you confirm which entity signs the marketplace contract? We need to know whether the agreement will be between Stratify Health and Redwood Inc. or via the cloud vendor intermediary.
- On the SOC2 artifacts: GC asked for the most recent penetration test summary (not full report). Can you provide that by EOD Friday?

Also, Tom asked whether you can commit to a pilot SLA for availability during the 8–12 week pilot (we don’t need commercial SLA, but a runbook with on-call coverage and a 4-hour incident acknowledgement window would be required).

We can confirm the 12/02 10:00–10:30AM PT slot pending Tom’s calendar — will let you know within the hour.

Best,
Priya
Head of Product Ops | Stratify Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: C-suite one-pager and short answers to your CFO/GC questions

Nice brief — +1 on the pilot credit and the 30-day termination clause. If Legal pushes too hard on Marketplace entity language, be prepared to move to SOW + PO and table a 10% starter discount for the pilot. I’ll own pricing redlines.

Also, Marcus: please turn the architecture diagram into a one-slide runbook (on-call steps + escalation path) for the workshop.

—Marissa
